Öland and the area south of Kalmar have a climate as mild as southern Skåne, and the Kalmar plain (Kalmarslätten) has high-quality arable land – 20,129 ha of arable land in the municipality (about 21% of the land area).

linneuniversitetet_ostersjoforskning.title: Linnaeus University and Baltic Sea research
linneuniversitetet_ostersjoforskning.text: Linnaeus University has 15,440 full-time equivalent students (2025), of whom about 6,000 are in Kalmar, and 49.5% of the municipality's 25–64-year-olds have post-secondary education. The university's Linnaeus Microbial Observatory has sampled the Baltic Sea off Kårehamn every other week since 2011 and the Kalmar Strait station every week since 2018, and the EEMiS research environment studies Baltic Sea ecology from microbes to fish and birds.

kalmarsundsverket.title: Kalmarsundsverket – water recycling on a large scale
kalmarsundsverket.text: Kalmar Vatten is building a new resource-recovery plant for just over SEK 2 billion, where up to 80% of the water will be reusable, for example for irrigation and as raw water; the water section will be commissioned in 2027. Discharges of nitrogen and phosphorus to the Kalmar Strait are expected to fall by at least 35%, and the plant will also produce biogas and biofertiliser.

kulturarv_slott_kvarnholmen.title: Kalmar Castle and the 17th-century town on Kvarnholmen
kulturarv_slott_kvarnholmen.text: Kalmar Castle was at the centre of events when the Kalmar Union was formed in 1397 and is described as Sweden's best-preserved Renaissance castle. From the 1650s the town was moved to Kvarnholmen as a fortified grid-plan town, with the cathedral designed by Nicodemus Tessin the Elder (1660–1682). At the same time, this historic environment is threatened by rising seas.

olandsbron_och_oland.title: The Öland Bridge, Öland and the World Heritage Site
olandsbron_och_oland.text: The Öland Bridge (6,072 m, opened in 1972) connects Kalmar with Öland. The Agricultural Landscape of Southern Öland has been a World Heritage Site since 2000 and covers over 56,000 ha, and Stora Alvaret (the Great Alvar) covers 250–260 km². The bridge is also a vulnerable link for food and water flows.

vaxande_jamlik_kommun.title: A growing, relatively equal municipality with high voter turnout
vaxande_jamlik_kommun.text: Kalmar Municipality is growing while the county is shrinking, has lower income inequality than Sweden as a whole (Gini 0.279 versus 0.314) and an almost even gender balance on the Municipal Council (49% women). Voter turnout in the 2026 municipal election was 84.6%, above the national figure of 82.3%.

agenda2030_och_gronstruktur.title: The 2030 Agenda in governance, and green space close at hand
agenda2030_och_gronstruktur.text: Both Kalmar Municipality and Region Kalmar County took part in Glokala Sverige (Glocal Sweden), and the Municipal Council's long-term goals are linked to the Global Goals. 94% of inhabitants in the Kalmar urban area have a green area within 200 metres, and a new green plan was adopted in April 2026 to strengthen green infrastructure, biodiversity and climate adaptation.

kommun_vision.title: Vision 2035 – Together we make a Kalmar for everyone even better and become Sweden's best municipality to live in
kommun_vision.text: The overarching vision of the municipal group, which all governance is based on. Among other things, it highlights quality of life, safety, clean water and fresh air, local food production, breaking fossil dependence, and Linnaeus University as an engine of development. The Municipal Council's long-term goals are linked to the 2030 Agenda.

kommun_vision.title: Comprehensive plan for 2035 with an outlook to 2050
kommun_vision.text: Adopted by the Municipal Council on 19 June 2023; gained legal force on 30 May 2025. One of its five strategic goals is a sustainable Kalmar at the forefront of environmental and climate work, with net-zero emissions by 2045 at the latest. New buildings must withstand flooding up to +2.8 m (RH2000).

kommun_vision.title: Climate-neutral Kalmar 2030 – Climate Contract 2030 (Viable Cities)
kommun_vision.text: Kalmar is one of 23 municipalities in Viable Cities' Climate Neutral Cities 2030 programme and has a climate contract with six national government agencies (2023 version). The goal is net-zero emissions by 2030, which means an 85% reduction compared with 1990 within the municipality's boundaries, and consumption-based emissions are included. In 2024, territorial emissions were 45% lower than in 1990.

kommun_vision.title: Action plan for a fossil-fuel-free municipality 2030
kommun_vision.text: Adopted by the Municipal Council in December 2019, replacing the climate and energy strategy. The goal “Fossil-fuel-free municipality 2030” has been in the municipality's operational plans since 2008 and refers to the entire municipality as a geographical area.

kommun_vision.title: Climate adaptation plan for Kalmar Municipality (version 1, updated 2025)
kommun_vision.text: Adopted by the Municipal Council on 29 November 2021 and editorially updated following a Municipal Council decision in February 2025. The plan is based on RCP8.5 and addresses sea level rise, cloudbursts, heat and drought. The city of Kalmar is identified by the Swedish Civil Contingencies Agency (MSB) as an area with significant flood risk.

kommun_vision.title: Mobility strategy for Kalmar Municipality
kommun_vision.text: The municipality's first mobility strategy (web page published in 2024). The goal is that by 2035, 60% of trips will be made on foot, by bicycle or by public transport, and 40% will be by car. Today, the car accounts for about 60% of travel.

kommun_vision.title: Green plan – thematic addendum to the comprehensive plan
kommun_vision.text: Adopted by the Municipal Council on 27 April 2026, replacing the green structure plan. It is intended to strengthen green infrastructure, biodiversity, health and climate adaptation, including protection against cloudbursts and heat.

kommun_vision.title: A Climate to Grow In – Regional development strategy for Kalmar County with an outlook to 2040
kommun_vision.text: Adopted by the Regional Council on 5 March 2026, with a clear link to the 2030 Agenda. Its priority areas are good and equal living conditions, sustainable and attractive living environments, and competitiveness and an innovative business sector.

kommun_vision.title: Fossil-fuel-free region 2030 – Action programme 2026–2028
kommun_vision.text: Since 2006, Kalmar County has had the goal of becoming a fossil-fuel-free region by 2030. The county is to produce at least as much renewable energy as it uses (excluding nuclear power). Interim targets are emissions at least 80% lower than in 1990 and at least 400 GWh of biogas by 2030.

kommun_vision.title: Climate and energy strategy for Kalmar County 2025–2030
kommun_vision.text: The vision is a fossil-fuel-free Kalmar County by 2030, with six focus areas and a tightened target of fossil-fuel-free transport by 2030 (published June 2025). Agriculture accounts for 43% of the county's greenhouse gas emissions.

kommun_vision.title: Growing Value – Regional food strategy for Kalmar County 2027–2036
kommun_vision.text: Successor to the food strategy for 2016–2025, developed by Region Kalmar County, LRF (Federation of Swedish Farmers) and the County Administrative Board. The vision is for Kalmar County to develop into a well-known, first-class food region.

kommun_vision.title: Regional water supply plan for Kalmar County 2024–2030
kommun_vision.text: Identifies water resources of regional importance and describes the water shortages in the county, including the drought years 2016, 2018 and 2022. The Baltic Sea is highlighted as a future water resource through desalination.
